summary: Shapiro et al. 2011 formalize exactly the merge/aggregation stage of any multi-agent pipeline: how concurrent contributions combine without central coordination. Core machinery: (1) A Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT) is a replicated data type whose design satisfies sufficient conditions for Strong Eventual Consistency (SEC); SEC = eventual consistency (eventual delivery, convergence, termination) plus Strong Convergence — correct replicas that have delivered the same updates have equivalent state immediately, with no consensus, no roll-back, and no waiting for quiescence (Defs. 2–3, page 4). (2) Two sufficient conditions: state-based CvRDT — payload forms a join semilattice, merge computes the least upper bound (commutative, idempotent, associative), and state is monotonically non-decreasing; Theorem 1 gives SEC assuming eventual delivery and termination (pages 4–5). Op-based CmRDT — updates split into a side-effect-free prepare step at the source and an effect-update delivered downstream; if all concurrent updates commute and delivery is reliable and causally ordered, Theorem 2 gives SEC (pages 5–6). (3) The two styles are mutually emulatable (Theorems 3–4, pages 7–8), so 'merge states' vs 'merge operations' is an implementation choice, not a difference in guarantee. (4) Scope and limits: SEC solves the CAP dilemma by staying available and partition-tolerant without consensus, tolerating n−1 crashes (page 6); but eventual delivery alone is insufficient (no-op merge counterexample, page 4), and SEC is incomparable with sequential consistency — the converged state need not correspond to any sequential execution (page 8). Crucially for the research note, the guarantees are truth-neutral: correctness is defined relative to a chosen concurrent specification, not relative to fact. Add-wins, remove-wins, highest-IP-wins, or reset-to-⊥ all satisfy strong convergence ('any of them may be reasonable for some application', page 8); LWW imposes a total order 'at the cost of losing concurrent updates' (page 13). Cross-paper inference for the note (not Shapiro's claim): both independent-sampling-plus-aggregation and staged Q/A must pick a merge rule for agent contributions, and CRDT theory shows that rule choice determines which contributions survive aggregation while saying nothing about whether the merged content is true — formally grounding the dossier constraint that agreement or merge success is not evidence of correctness. A further diagnostic for the note: LLM free-text synthesis is generally neither commutative nor idempotent, so it fails the CRDT sufficient conditions and inherits no convergence guarantee at all.
unresolved: Whether any aggregation operator actually used in multi-agent LLM systems (majority vote, evidence-union, LLM free-text synthesis) satisfies commutativity/idempotence/monotonicity; LLM synthesis plausibly violates all three, meaning staged Q/A and independent+aggregation pipelines may have no convergence guarantee of the CRDT kind — a diagnostic the research note should exploit but this extraction cannot settle.
The paper gives no guidance on merging weighted, probabilistic, or natural-language content; adapting semilattice machinery to confidence-bearing claims is open.
